name: ExecV3
description:
Run commands with structured input — no shell, no quoting, no string-splitting.

Give a flat `commands` list. Each command joins the NEXT via its `op`:
  • absent  → sequential (run next regardless)        bash: `;`
  • "&&"    → run next only if this succeeds           bash: `&&`
  • "||"    → run next only if this fails              bash: `||`
  • "|"     → pipe this stdout into the next stdin     bash: `|`

Precedence is bash's, exactly: "|" binds tightest, then "&&"/"||" (equal, left to
right). `a && b || c` means `(a && b) || c`. Omit `op` on the last command.

`results` has one slot per command, position-aligned to `commands` (results[i] is
commands[i]); a command that was short-circuited (skipped) is `null`, so read it
defensively (results[i]?.exitCode). `success` is the exit status of the last command
that actually ran, bash-style. Per-command exit/stderr is always in `results`, so a
pipe's per-stage truth is never lost.

Anything needing grouping, variables, `$(...)`, loops or globbing is a script — write
it to a file and run the file. Redirect is overwrite-only ({ stdout, stderr }; stderr
"&1" folds 2>&1); append/fd-level redirects are a script.

intent.description: Your intent for this run: the goal, not a restatement of the command. E.g. "confirm the build is green before tagging", not "run pnpm build".
examples: count the TODO markers in the tree

program.description: The program, binary, or script path to execute. Supports ~ and $VAR expansion. Must be on $PATH or an absolute path — no shell expansion of globs or operators.

args.description: Arguments to the program. Each argument is a separate string — no shell quoting. ~ and $VAR are NOT expanded in args.

op.description: How THIS command joins the NEXT one (forward-pointing). "&&" run next if this succeeds; "||" run next if this fails; "|" pipe this stdout into next stdin. Absent = sequential (run next regardless). Bash precedence: "|" binds tightest, then "&&"/"||" (equal, left-associative). Omit on the last command.

cwd.description: Working directory for this command. Supports ~ and $VAR expansion.

env.description: Environment variables to set for this command (merged over the inherited environment).

stdin.description: Literal stdin for this command (here-string / heredoc equivalent). Not allowed on the target of a pipe — the pipe owns stdin.

redirect.description: Redirect this command's stdout/stderr to files

stdout.description: Redirect stdout to this file path (overwrite). ~ and $VAR expanded. For append or fd-level redirects, use a script.

stderr.description: Redirect stderr to a file path, OR the literal "&1" to merge stderr into wherever stdout goes (2>&1). ~ and $VAR expanded.

commands.description: Flat list of commands, joined by each command's forward-pointing `op`. One command = run it. A simple chain or a pipe stays flat — no nesting. Anything needing grouping, variables, substitution, loops or globbing is a script, not this tool.

stripAnsi.description: Strip ANSI escape codes from output (default true).

input_examples.intent: build, then run the tests only if the build passed
count the TODO markers in the tree
build, capturing stdout and stderr together into one log file
lint then test, and announce if either step fails
collect and sort the TODO markers from one package into a file
